info.title: Voices.az API
info.description:
Text-to-speech, speech-to-text and video dubbing over HTTP.

Every account gets an API key at registration. The key identifies the account, and
everything it creates is billed to that account's balance — so a call that would cost
more than the remaining balance is refused before any work is queued.

**Base URL** — `https://voices.az/api`

### Authentication

Send the key in the `X-API-KEY` header on every request:

```
X-API-KEY: vz_live_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
```

For compatibility with the published PHP client the key is also accepted as a bare
`Authorization` header (no `Bearer` prefix). New integrations should use `X-API-KEY`.

The key must never travel in a query string: it would end up in server logs, in proxy
logs and in the `Referer` of every asset a response links to. Requests carrying a key
in the URL are refused with `401`.

Keys are managed in the panel at **app.voices.az → Profile → API key**: the current
key is shown there, and it can be rotated or revoked. Rotation is immediate — the
previous key stops working the moment the new one is issued — and the new secret is
displayed once.

### What a key may call

A key authenticates the *integration* surface and nothing else. Everything documented
in this reference is inside that surface:

* the service endpoints — `/services/text-to-speech/*`, `/services/speech-to-text/*`,
  `/services/dubbing/*`, `/services/cloning/*`, `/services/website-reader/*`;
* the catalogue — `/languages`, `/get-languages`, `/get-voices`, `/get-voice/*`,
  `/services`, `/service/{slug}`, `/favorite`;
* read-only account figures — `/customer/balance`, `/customer/transactions`.

Everything else on `app.voices.az` is a panel-session operation and is refused to a
key with `403` and `error.type = api_key_scope`: the profile and its updates, the
avatar, panel state, logout, balance top-ups, promo codes, and the API key's own
lifecycle (show / rotate / revoke). A key that leaks can therefore cost its owner
balance — it can never take over the account, read the owner's contact details, or
replace itself.

Sign in to the panel for any of those. There is no way to widen a key's scope.

### Idempotency

Every call that queues work debits the balance, so a retry after a network timeout
must not become a second charge. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header on those calls:

```
Idempotency-Key: 8e6c3f0a-2a7d-4a5e-9f2b-7b1c0d4e5a66
```

* **Same key, same body** — the stored response is replayed unchanged, with the same
  `request_id` and the header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Nothing is queued and
  nothing is charged a second time.
* **Same key, different body** — `422`, `error.type = idempotency_key_reused`. The key
  already stands for a different operation; use a new one.
* **Same key while the first call is still running** — `409`,
  `error.type = idempotency_in_progress`. Wait a moment and retry with the same key to
  get the replay.
* **Server errors are not stored.** If a call fails with `5xx`, retrying it with the
  same key runs the operation for real.

Records live for **24 hours**. The key may be any string of up to 64 characters from
`A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ : -`; a uuid per operation is the intended use. Anything longer or
outside that set is refused with `422`, `error.type = idempotency_key_invalid`.

The header is honoured on the calls that charge:

| Endpoint |
| --- |
| `POST /services/text-to-speech/synthesize` |
| `POST /services/text-to-speech/generate/{projectId}` |
| `POST /services/speech-to-text/init` |
| `POST /services/speech-to-text/recognize` |
| `POST /services/speech-to-text/generate/{projectId}` |
| `POST /services/dubbing/init` |
| `POST /services/dubbing/preview/{projectId}` |
| `POST /services/dubbing/generate/{projectId}` |
| `POST /services/dubbing/render/{projectId}` |
| `POST /services/dubbing/regenerate-chunk/{projectId}/{chunkId}` |

Everywhere else the header is ignored, so a client may send it on every request
without keeping track of which endpoints honour it. Without the header, behaviour is
unchanged.

### Pricing

The API bills at exactly the same per-minute tariff as the panel — there is no
surcharge for API use and no separate API plan. The current rate per service is
`GET /services` and `GET /service/{slug}`; what a specific run will cost is returned
by the call that starts it (`price`), and the charge is taken from the same balance
the panel spends. Duration is billed per minute of processed audio or video.

### Retention

Files do not live in storage forever. The **project row** does: an expired project
keeps its id, its title and its place in `get-projects`, and
`GET /services/{service}/{projectId}` still answers `200`. What it loses is its files.

| What | Window |
| --- | --- |
| A paid project of any service, and everything it produced | **6 months** (180 days) after the last activity on it |
| A dubbing project that was only previewed and never paid for | **30 days** |
| Cloned voices | never swept |

"Last activity" is the latest of the project's creation, its last change and its last
order.

Once the sweep has taken a project's files it is marked, on every endpoint that returns
a project:

* `is_expired: true`
* `expired_at` — when the files went, ISO-8601

and every url under `body` is `null`, so a client that ignores the flag gets nulls
rather than links to objects that are gone.

Any call that would ACT on those files answers `410` with `error.type = gone`:

| Refused with `410` |
| --- |
| `POST /services/text-to-speech/generate/{projectId}` |
| `POST /services/text-to-speech/export/{projectId}` |
| `POST /services/speech-to-text/generate/{projectId}` |
| `POST /services/speech-to-text/export/{projectId}` |
| `POST /services/dubbing/generate/{projectId}` |
| `POST /services/dubbing/preview/{projectId}` |
| `POST /services/dubbing/regenerate-chunk/{projectId}/{chunkId}` |
| `POST /services/dubbing/render/{projectId}` |
| `POST /services/dubbing/export/{projectId}` |

Reading, listing, renaming, favouriting and deleting an expired project keep working,
and creating a NEW project from the same text or a fresh upload is never affected.
Retrying a `410` never helps — the files cannot be restored. Download what matters
before the window closes.

### Text tags

Text sent to text-to-speech may carry a few inline tags. They are written in square
brackets, inside the `text` field itself:

| Tag | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `[PAUSE=1.5]` | A silence of that many seconds at this point. |
| `[LAUGH]` | A short laugh. |
| `[SIGH]` | A sigh. |
| `[UHM]` | An "uhm" hesitation, as in live speech. |
| `[SHH]` | A quiet "shh". |

`[PAUSE=n]` takes its length in seconds with a decimal point — `[PAUSE=0.5]`,
`[PAUSE=1.5]`. Anything shorter than half a second is not treated as a pause.

Tag names are case-insensitive: `[laugh]` and `[LAUGH]` are the same tag. Anything
else between square brackets is not a tag — unknown tags are removed from the text
before synthesis, so they are never read out.

The four sound tags are a hint rather than an instruction: they mark where the sound
belongs, and the AI may mispronounce them.

Tags are part of the text, so they count towards the character limit of the `text`
field. They do not change the price: text-to-speech is billed by the duration of the
audio that comes back, and the silence of a `[PAUSE=n]` is part of that duration.

### Language

`Accept-Language: az | en | ru | tr` selects the language of human-readable messages
(`message`, `error.message`, status titles). It does not affect ids or enum values.

### Response envelope

Every response uses the same envelope.

Success:

```json
{ "success": true, "message": "Operation successful", "data": { } }
```

Failure:

```json
{
  "success": false,
  "error": { "message": "…", "code": 404, "type": "not_found", "data": null }
}
```

`error.code` is the HTTP status; `error.type` is a stable machine-readable slug —
branch on that rather than on the message, which is localised.

### Rate limits

60 requests per minute and 5000 per day, counted per API key. Over budget the API
answers `429` with `Retry-After` and `X-RateLimit-*` headers. Back off for
`Retry-After` seconds; do not retry immediately.

### Asynchronous work

Synthesis, recognition and dubbing are queued. The call that starts one returns a
`request_id`; poll the matching `get-response` endpoint (or, for speech-to-text, the
project itself) until `status` becomes `COMPLETED` or `FAILED`. Poll no more often
than once every 2 seconds.

tags.name: Text to speech
tags.description: Turn text into an audio file.

tags.name: Speech to text
tags.description: Turn an audio or video source into text and subtitles.

tags.name: Dubbing
tags.description: Replace the speech in a video with speech in another language.

get.description:
The `id` values returned here are what `language_id` expects everywhere else.
This endpoint needs no key.
Public voices plus any voice the account owns. Paginated, 20 per page.

parameters.name: language_id
parameters.description: Only voices that support this language.

get.description:
One entry per service (`text-to-speech`, `speech-to-text`, `dubbing`, …) with the
current tariff. `price.amount` is per minute of produced audio or video, in
`price.currency`.

`GET /service/{slug}` returns the same entry for one service, and adds what only
that service has: its `limits` and, for dubbing, `prices` - the rates charged
BESIDE the tariff. Dubbing has one, `auto_emotion_per_min`: the per-minute
surcharge for picking the emotion of every line automatically, billed on the same
minutes as the dub itself.

`auto_emotion_per_min` is nullable: `null` means the operator has switched the
automatic emotion off site-wide, so the feature is not on offer - clients hide the
switch, and `auto_emotion` is forced to `false` wherever it is accepted.

services.title: Text to speech
services.description: Convert written text into natural speech.
services.instruction: Paste your text, pick a voice, generate.

services.title: Dubbing
services.description: Dub a video into another language.
services.instruction: Upload a video or paste a link, pick the languages.

post.summary: Synthesize a single piece of text
post.description:
The one-call entry point: creates a project, adds the text and queues it.
Returns a `request_id` to poll.

Charging happens on download (`export`), not here.

get.description:
Poll until `status` is `COMPLETED` or `FAILED`. While it is `IN_PROGRESS` the
response carries `percentage` (0–100).

A `request_id` that does not belong to the account is answered exactly like an
unknown one — a neutral `IN_PROGRESS` at 0 %.

post.summary: Charge for and download the audio
post.description:
Charges the account for the project the first time it is called and returns the
audio file URL. Calling it again on an already paid project does not charge twice.

The delivered file is MP3. A `format` field is accepted for backwards
compatibility and ignored.

Answers `410` once the project's retention window has passed — see **Retention**.

422.description: Not enough balance, or nothing to export.

error.message: Your balance is not sufficient for this operation.

post.summary: Add a text block to a project
post.description:
Use this to build a multi-block project. Omit `project_id` to start a new one; the
response carries the id to use for the following blocks.

text.description:
May contain the inline tags described under **Text tags** —
`[PAUSE=1.5]`, `[LAUGH]`, `[SIGH]`, `[UHM]`, `[SHH]`. They count
towards `maxLength`; unknown tags are removed before synthesis.

put.summary: Update a block's text and speed

text.description:
May contain the inline tags described under **Text tags** —
`[PAUSE=1.5]`, `[LAUGH]`, `[SIGH]`, `[UHM]`, `[SHH]`. They count
towards `maxLength`; unknown tags are removed before synthesis.

post.description:
Returns the `request_id` to poll on `get-response`.

Answers `410` once the project's retention window has passed — see **Retention**.

post.summary: Recognize an audio file or a YouTube video
post.description:
Creates the project, charges the account and queues the run in one call. Send
either `voice` (an uploaded file, `multipart/form-data`) or `youtube_url` — exactly
one of the two.

Poll `GET /services/speech-to-text/{projectId}` and read `body.percentage` until
the project's `status` reaches `Completed` (3) or `Rejected` (5).

voice.description: Audio or video file. Accepted formats and the size ceiling come from `GET /service/speech-to-text`.

youtube_url.description: A YouTube watch URL. Mutually exclusive with `voice`.

language_id.description: Language spoken in the source, from `GET /languages`.

diarize.description: Number of speakers to separate. `1` disables separation.

demucs.description: Strip music and background noise first. Improves the result on noisy sources and makes the run slower.

convert_numbers.description: Write numbers as digits instead of words.

422.description: Validation failed, or the balance does not cover the run.

error.message: Your balance is not sufficient for this operation.

post.summary: Upload a source without starting recognition
post.description:
Two-step alternative to `recognize`: upload first, read back the detected duration
and the quote, then start the run with `generate`.

project_id.description: Replace the source of an existing draft.

post.summary: Start recognition on an uploaded source
post.description: Answers `410` once the project's retention window has passed — see **Retention**.

get.description:
This is also the polling endpoint: while the run is going `status.id` is
`2` (In progress) and `body.percentage` climbs to 100.

post.description:
Renders the transcript in the requested format and returns a URL to it. Unknown
formats are refused.

Answers `410` once the project's retention window has passed — see **Retention**.

post.summary: Create a dubbing project from a file or a YouTube URL
post.description:
Creates a draft and starts preparing the source. Nothing is charged here.

Send either `file` or `youtube_url`. The accepted formats and the size ceiling are
in `GET /services/dubbing/get-formats`.

source_language_id.description: Language spoken in the source. Detected automatically when omitted.

language_id.description: Language to dub into. Required by the time `generate` is called.

background_mode.description:
How the original soundtrack is handled under the new speech.
`duck` lowers it while a line plays; `demucs` separates music and
effects from speech and keeps them at full level.

overlap_pan.description: Pan overlapping speakers apart in the stereo field.

auto_emotion.description:
Pick the emotion of every line automatically and voice it with the
matching style of the speaker's voice. Carries a per-minute surcharge
on top of the dubbing tariff - `prices.auto_emotion_per_min` in the
service payload - charged once, with the first `generate`. Can also be
turned on later, through the settings endpoint.

Stored as `false` whatever is sent while the operator has the feature
switched off (`prices.auto_emotion_per_min` is then `null`).

get.summary: List accepted source formats and background modes

put.description:
`background_mode` and `overlap_pan` are applied at mix time, so changing them never
invalidates work already done. `auto_emotion` changes how the lines are voiced, so
the next `render` re-records the ones it affects.

auto_emotion.description:
Pick the emotion of every line automatically (see `init`). Changing it
charges nothing by itself and queues nothing: the lines it affects are
re-recorded by the next `render`, which is also where the surcharge is
taken if the project has not paid it yet.

post.description:
Runs the first seconds of the video through the whole pipeline so the result can be
judged before paying for the full dub. A number of previews per project are free;
beyond that each one is charged at the rate shown in the panel. Only allowed while
the project is a draft.

Returns a `request_id` to poll on `get-response`. Answers `410` once the
project's retention window has passed — see **Retention**.

Charges the account for the full dub and queues it. Poll `get-response` until
`status` is `COMPLETED`.

`voice_map` assigns a voice to each detected speaker. Leave it out to let every
speaker keep a default voice of matching gender.

This is the call that pays for the dub: it sets the project's `is_paid` to `true`,
and `POST /services/dubbing/export/{projectId}` is free from then on.

The amount is the per-minute dubbing tariff x the billable minutes, plus the
automatic-emotion surcharge when `body.auto_emotion` is on and has not been paid
for yet (`prices.auto_emotion_per_min` in the service payload x the same minutes).
It is a single order line and a single debit.

Answers `410` once the project's retention window has passed — see **Retention**.

auto_emotion.description:
Pick the emotion of every line automatically. When it is on at this
call, its per-minute surcharge is part of the amount charged here -
one order line, one debit - and is never charged again.

voice_map.description: Speaker key to voice. Keys come from `body.speakers` of the project.

get.description:
Takes the `request_id` of any dubbing run — a preview, a full dub, a render, a
single re-recorded line, or the mp4 assembly behind a `202` from `export` — and
reports its stage and percentage.

`video_url` is `null` for every run since 2026-09-15: a render produces the
soundtrack, and the downloadable mp4 is built by `export`. An id that does not
belong to the account is answered exactly like an unknown one — a neutral
`IN_PROGRESS` at 0 %.

`body.chunks` holds the per-line timeline: source text, translation, timing and the
voice-over for each line. `body.speakers` holds the detected speakers and the keys
`voice_map` expects.

This is also where an export is watched: `body.export_status` and
`body.export_request_id` report the mp4 assembly started by
`POST /services/dubbing/export/{projectId}`.

**Media urls.** `audio_url` — and `video_url` where a project still has one — carry
a `?v=…` cache-buster that changes with every render. Use the url exactly as it is
given: the object behind it is overwritten in place, and a url with the stamp
stripped can serve the previous render for hours.

`video_url` is `null` for every project rendered since 2026-09-15: a render now
produces the soundtrack only, and the picture is the source the project was created
from (`source_video_url` for a YouTube source, otherwise the uploaded file). Play
`audio_url` over the source, and use `export` for a single muxed file. Older
projects keep whatever `video_url` they had.

request_id.description: The most recent run of this project, or `null`.

exporting.description:
What the project looks like between the `202` of `export` and the `200`
of the next call. `export_status` clears when the file is there.

expired.description:
The project is still readable and still listed; its urls are `null` and
generate / preview / regenerate-chunk / render / export answer `410`.

put.description:
Changing `trans`, `speed` or the voice marks the line for re-recording; the next
`render` picks it up.

Picking a `voice` here is a manual choice and wins over the automatic emotion: it
clears the line's `vo.auto_style`, and the next take is recorded with the voice
sent here. Sending `voice: null` gives that choice back — the line returns to its
speaker's voice and to the automatic emotion.

voice.description:
The voice this one line is recorded with. `null` removes it: the line
goes back to the voice of its speaker, and to the automatic emotion if
the project uses it.

post.description: Answers `410` once the project's retention window has passed — see **Retention**.

A number of renders per project are free; beyond that each one is charged at the
rate shown in the panel. Returns a `request_id` to poll.

`data.price` is the WHOLE amount this render costs, or `null` when it costs
nothing. Besides the re-render fee it may carry one more thing, once: the
automatic-emotion surcharge, when `body.auto_emotion` was switched on after the dub
had already been paid for. It is taken by the first render that follows, after
which `body.auto_emotion_paid_at` is set and the switch is free to turn off and on
again.

A render produces the soundtrack, not a video file: `body.audio_url` is rewritten
(with a fresh `?v=` stamp) and `body.video_url` stays `null`. The downloadable mp4
is built on demand by `export`.

Answers `410` once the project's retention window has passed — see **Retention**.

Returns the final video and audio, without the preview watermark. The dub is paid
for on `generate` (`is_paid: true` on the project), so this call normally charges
nothing; a project dubbed before that rule is charged here, once.

**The mp4 is built on demand, so this endpoint has two successes.** A render leaves
the soundtrack behind, not a muxed file, so the first export of a project usually
has to assemble one:

* `200` — the file is ready. `data` carries `title`, `file` (mp4) and `audio`
  (mp3).
* `202` — `data` is `{ "pending": true, "request_id": "…" }`. The assembly was
  queued. Calling again while it runs returns the SAME `202` and the same
  `request_id`; it never queues a second one.

**How to poll.** Watch the project itself:
`GET /services/dubbing/{projectId}` → `body.export_status` is `pending` while the
mp4 is being assembled, `failed` if that attempt died, and `null` once it is done;
`body.export_request_id` is the id of that attempt. When `export_status` clears,
call `export` again and it answers `200`. `GET /services/dubbing/get-response/{requestId}`
takes the same `request_id` and reports the stage and percentage while it runs.
A `failed` status is not fatal — the next `export` starts a fresh attempt. Poll no
more often than once every 2 seconds.

**The urls carry a `?v=…` cache-buster and must be used exactly as given.** The
objects behind them are overwritten in place by the next render, so a url with the
stamp stripped can serve the previous render for hours. The mp4 is a cache with a
short life of its own: an export that is not fetched promptly may have to be
assembled again — which is simply another `202`, not an error.

Answers `410` once the project's retention window has passed — see **Retention**.

202.description:
The mp4 is being assembled. Poll the project's `body.export_status` and call
again when it clears. Nothing is charged for a `202`.

422.description:
Nothing to export, or the balance does not cover an export that still has to be
paid for.

"Nothing to export" is final rather than a "not yet": either the project has no
video to hand over and none can be built (an audio-only source), or it has not
been rendered. Render it first; retrying the export alone will not change the
answer.

nothingToExport.summary: No video, and none can be assembled

error.message: There is no rendered video to export yet. Render the project first.

balance.summary: An unpaid dub the balance does not cover

error.message: Your balance is not sufficient for this operation.

ApiKeyAuth.name: X-API-KEY
ApiKeyAuth.description:
The account's API key, from **app.voices.az → Profile → API key**.
Also accepted as a bare `Authorization` header (no `Bearer` prefix) for
compatibility with the published PHP client. Never send it in a query string.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description:
Makes this call safe to retry. See **Idempotency** in the introduction.

Use a fresh value (a uuid) per operation you want performed once. Sending the same
value again with the same body replays the first response and carries
`Idempotent-Replayed: true`; with a different body it answers `422`
(`idempotency_key_reused`); while the first call is still running it answers `409`
(`idempotency_in_progress`). Records are kept for 24 hours.

message.description: Human-readable, localised by `Accept-Language`. Do not branch on it.

ProjectStatus.description:
`1` Draft · `2` In progress · `3` Completed · `4` Ordered · `5` Rejected ·
`6` Waiting for ordering.

Project.description:
The shape every project-returning endpoint hands back — the `get-projects` lists of
all three services, the single-project read, and the calls that echo the project
back after a write (`init`, `update-title`, the dubbing settings). `body` is
service-specific and is shown in the examples of that service's own endpoints.

is_expired.description:
The project outlived its retention window and its files were deleted — see
**Retention**. The project itself is still here and still listed, but every url
under `body` is `null` and the calls that touch files answer `410`.

expired_at.description:
When the files were deleted, ISO-8601 with offset
(`"2026-03-18T04:00:11+04:00"`). `null` while the project still has them, so it
is `null` exactly when `is_expired` is `false`.

is_paid.description:
The project's own price has already been charged, so handing the files over
does not charge again.

For dubbing that happens on the first full `generate`, and
`POST /services/dubbing/export/{projectId}` is free from then on. A dub made
before that rule carries no such marker and is charged on its first export
instead, so it reads `false` until that export goes through. For the services
that charge on download it turns `true` together with the `Ordered` (4) status.

duration.description: Seconds of processed audio or video.

price.description: Omitted entirely while the project has no quote yet.

body.description: Service-specific payload. Every url in it is `null` on an expired project.

DubbingBody.description:
`body` of a dubbing project. Read-only: everything in it is written by the
pipeline, not by the client.

The watermark-free files and the secret directory they live under are deliberately
absent — they are handed out by `POST /services/dubbing/export/{projectId}` alone.
So is the render's own clock: `rendered_at` is NOT part of the payload, and the only
thing a client needs from it is already applied, as the `?v=` stamp on the urls.

source_path.description: Storage key of the source the project was created from.

youtube_url.description: The source URL, for a project created from YouTube.

source_video_url.description:
Playable copy of the original video, stored for a YouTube source once it has
been downloaded. `null` for an uploaded source.

video_url.description:
`null` for every project rendered since 2026-09-15 — a render produces the
soundtrack only, and the downloadable mp4 is assembled on demand by `export`.
Play `audio_url` over the source video instead. Projects rendered earlier keep
the url they had. Carries a `?v=` stamp when present; use it as given.

audio_url.description:
The dubbed soundtrack of the last render, with the preview watermark. The
`?v=` suffix is a cache-buster that changes with every render: the object is
overwritten in place, so a url with the stamp stripped can serve the previous
render for hours. Use the url exactly as it is given.

auto_emotion.description:
Whether the emotion of every line is picked automatically and voiced with the
matching style of the speaker's voice.

auto_emotion_paid_at.description:
When the surcharge for it was charged, or `null` while it is still owed. It is
taken once - with the first `generate` if the switch was on by then, otherwise
with the next `render` - and after that the switch costs nothing to change.

stage.description: Pipeline stage of the last run — `preview_ready` after a preview, `done` after a full dub.

preview_audio_url.description: Preview soundtrack of older projects, kept for compatibility.

estimate.description:
Volume figures measured while preparing the source. Informative only — the
price is the per-minute dubbing tariff and is reported as the project's `price`.

render_count.description: Renders already used, so a client can say "N of M free" before starting one.

export_status.description:
State of the LAST mp4 assembly started by `POST /services/dubbing/export/{projectId}`.

* `pending` — an assembly is running; `export` answers `202` with the same
  `export_request_id`.
* `failed` — that attempt died. The next `export` starts a fresh one; the
  project itself is unaffected.
* `no_video` — the source has no video track at all, so there is nothing to
  assemble, ever; `export` answers `422`.
* `null` — nothing to report. After a successful assembly the field clears, and
  the next `export` answers `200` with the file.

export_request_id.description:
The run id of that assembly, the same value `export` returned with its `202`.
Usable with `GET /services/dubbing/get-response/{requestId}` for stage and
percentage.

speakers.description: Detected speakers. The `key` of each is what `voice_map` expects.

chunks.description:
The per-line timeline - source text, translation, timing, voice-over.

Two fields on a line are about the emotion: `emotion` (`{label, score}`,
measured on the source voice of that line and present whether or not the
automatic selection is on - `unknown` when the line is too short to judge) and
`vo.auto_style`, the style that was picked automatically for the take that is
currently there. `vo.auto_style` is absent when the take was recorded with the
speaker's own voice or with one chosen by hand.

file.description:
The muxed mp4, without the watermark. Carries a `?v=` cache-buster — use the
url exactly as given.

audio.description: The soundtrack alone, without the watermark. Same `?v=` rule.

DubbingExportPending.description:
The `202` payload of `POST /services/dubbing/export/{projectId}`: no file yet, one
is being assembled.

pending.description: Always `true`. Its presence is what distinguishes a `202` body from a `200` one.

request_id.description:
The assembly's run id, mirrored into the project as `body.export_request_id`.
A second `export` while it is running returns this same id.

language_id.description: From `GET /languages`. Defaults to the site language.

voice_id.description: From `GET /get-voices`. Defaults to a public voice of the chosen language.

Unauthorized.description:
Missing, unknown, revoked or query-string-borne API key, or an account that is not
active.

NotFound.description:
No such resource, or it belongs to another account — the API does not distinguish
the two.

Gone.description:
The project outlived its retention window: its files were deleted and this call
acts on them — see **Retention** in the introduction. The project itself is still
readable, still listed and still renamable; only the file operations are refused,
and retrying never helps because the files cannot be restored.

`error.data` carries the project id and the moment the files went — the same value
the project's own `expired_at` reports.

error.message: This project's retention period has ended and its files were deleted

IdempotencyInProgress.description:
Another request with the same `Idempotency-Key` is still being processed. Wait for
it to finish and retry with the same key — the retry will replay its response.

error.message: A request with this Idempotency-Key is still being processed. Retry in a few seconds.

ValidationError.description: The request did not pass validation.

TooManyRequests.description:
Over the per-key budget (60 requests/minute, 5000/day). Wait `Retry-After`
seconds.

error.message: Too many attempts. Please try again later.
